questionText:
Consider the C function foo and the binary tree shown.

When foo is called with a pointer to the root node of the given binary tree, what will it print?
explanation:
Step-by-step Execution:

The function foo(p) recursively calculates the sum of the node's value and the values returned by its left and right subtrees, then prints retval before returning it.

1. foo(10) calls foo(5) and foo(11):
• foo(5) calls foo(3) and foo(8):
    - foo(3): $p \rightarrow \text{left} = \text{NULL}$, $p \rightarrow \text{right} = \text{NULL}$. Returns $3 + 0 + 0 = 3$. Prints 3.
    - foo(8): $p \rightarrow \text{left} = \text{NULL}$, $p \rightarrow \text{right} = \text{NULL}$. Returns $8 + 0 + 0 = 8$. Prints 8.
    - foo(5) returns $5 + 3 + 8 = 16$. Prints 16.

• foo(11) calls foo(NULL) and foo(13):
    - foo(NULL) returns $0$.
    - foo(13) returns $13 + 0 + 0 = 13$. Prints 13.
    - foo(11) returns $11 + 0 + 13 = 24$. Prints 24.

• foo(10) returns $10 + 16 + 24 = 50$. Prints 50.

The printed order is: 3 8 16 13 24 50.
